name: Introduction and overview — F/A-18 Hornet — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — F/A-18 Hornet
description: Introduction and overview of the F/A-18 Hornet: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The F/A-18 Hornet is a twin-engine carrier-capable multirole fighter built by McDonnell Douglas (now Boeing), entering service in 1983. Designed from the start as both fighter and attack aircraft, it replaced the F-4, A-4, and A-7 in Navy and Marine Corps service. About 1,480 Hornets were built before production shifted to the larger Super Hornet. Baseline facts: Twin-engine carrier multirole fighter; service from 1983; ~1,480 built by McDonnell Douglas/Boeing..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: F/A-18 Hornet: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Twin-engine carrier multirole fighter; service from 1983; ~1,480 built by McDonnell Douglas/Boeing.
